verdict.rationale: GitLab's documentation covers secret detection, push protection, recording exposures in the vulnerability report, and automatic revocation for some secret types. None of the evidence shows detected secrets being checked against the issuing service to tell whether they are live. Revocation is a related but different control, so it earns no credit for this story.

support.subject: As a security-engineer, I can have detected secrets verified against the issuing service so I know which ones are live
